sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the novelty that although teshuvah involves the makifim of Chayah and Yechidah, which are wondrous and distant from Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah, through contemplation within NRN one can awaken these makifim and even the higher makifim of Arich and Atik.

translations.translation: And it needs to be understood,
what does the verse innovate in this, that this mitzvah
(teshuvah)
is not wondrous for you nor distant from you,
for seemingly,
since also in man,
the service of teshuvah is in the makifim of Chayah and Yechidah,
which are analogous to the makifim above
(Arich and Atik),
what is the innovation
(so much)
in this, that through service in the makifim of the soul, the makifim above are drawn down?
And it may be said,
that "from you" refers to Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah, which are the essence of man43.
For although teshuvah is in the makifim of the soul,
nevertheless,
in order to arouse the makifim, there must be contemplation,
and the contemplation
(which is in NRN)
must be in a manner that through this the makifim that are above intellect will be aroused.
And this is the innovation in "it is not wondrous for you etc.," that "from you" refers to NRN
(as above),
for although the makifim of Chayah and Yechidah are wondrous and distant from NRN,
nevertheless,
it is within the power of NRN to arouse
(through appropriate contemplation)
the makifim of Chayah and Yechidah44,
and through them also the makifim above,
Arich and Atik.
And the reason for this is
(as brought above
(end of section 4)
from the maamar)
because the souls of Yisrael
(that is, also the NRN)
have everything,
and also from above they are given everything.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two terms "wondrous" and "distant" in the verse correspond to two aspects of mitzvos: the Divine will beyond reason (wondrous) and the reasons for mitzvos within Chochmah (distant).

translations.translation: And this will be understood by prefacing that the precise explanation of the verse's wording "it is not wondrous from you"
(specifically "from you"),
is also according to the interpretation45
that "this mitzvah" refers to all the mitzvos in general.
For also according to this interpretation,
"this mitzvah" is in the category of wonder,
and as brought above
(section 4)
from the maamar,
that also all the mitzvos,
being the Supernal Will that is above reason,
are in the category of wonder and distance
(except that nevertheless it is not wondrous from you,
from Yisrael).
And it may be said,
that this which it says two terms,
"wondrous" and "distant,"
is,
because in mitzvos there are two matters.
This, that the mitzvos are His will,
a will that is above reason.
And this, that after the will becomes clothed in Chochmah
(of Torah),
a reason is also added for each mitzvah46.
And these are the two terms of wonder and distance,
for the will in the mitzvos,
being above reason,
is wonder.
And the reasons for the mitzvos as they are from the aspect of the Chochmah of Torah as it is above,
are in the category of distance.
For although also the reasons for the mitzvos
(as they are in His Chochmah)
are above the comprehension of human intellect47,
nevertheless,
the Chochmah above is the source for the Chochmah and intellect of created beings48,
and therefore it is not wondrous from the intellect of created beings, only distant from them49.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the terms "wondrous" and "distant" only apply after the Torah and mitzvos have descended into a relationship with the world, not in their essential state.

translations.translation: And it may be added,
that the mitzvos and Torah
(the reasons for the mitzvos)
as they are in their own essence,
it is not applicable to say of them even the description of wonder and distance.
For the term wonder
(and certainly the term distance)
indicates that the wondrous thing has some connection to the thing from which it is wondrous.
But regarding two matters that have no connection between them,
the term wonder does not apply.
Just as it is not applicable to say of a logical concept that it is wondrous from the sense of touch50.
And that the Torah and mitzvos are distant and wondrous is after they have descended to have some connection to the world.
For the beginning of the descent is that the Torah preceded the world.
For the Torah as it is in its own essence,
is not in the category of worlds at all, and it is not applicable to say of it that it preceded the world.
And that which our sages said51
"Two thousand years the Torah preceded the world,"
is in the level of Torah as it descended52
to be in the category of worlds.
For in this level it is applicable to say that it preceded the world,
and moreover,
there is a measure to its precedence,
two thousand years.
And after this it descended yet many more descents53,
until it was drawn down below.
And in this level of Torah,
as it is after its descent
[which is a general level,
including many particular levels,
from the level of Torah that preceded the world until the level of Torah that was drawn down below]
it is applicable to say that it is in the category of wonder and distance.
